events.title: Henry III of England marries Eleanor of Provence
events.description: Henry III married the twelve-year-old Eleanor of Provence at Canterbury Cathedral. Her many relatives at court provoked resentment among English barons in the years before the Second Barons' War.
events.html: Henry III married the twelve-year-old Eleanor of Provence at Canterbury Cathedral. Her many relatives at court provoked resentment among English barons in the years before the Second Barons' War.

events.title: Death of Andrew III ends Hungary's Árpád dynasty
events.description: Andrew III died without a son, ending the male line of the Árpád dynasty, which had led the Magyars since the conquest of the Carpathian Basin. Years of succession war followed.
events.html: Andrew III died without a son, ending the male line of the Árpád dynasty, which had led the Magyars since the conquest of the Carpathian Basin. Years of succession war followed.

events.title: Connecticut adopts the Fundamental Orders
events.description: Settlers of Hartford, Windsor and Wethersfield agreed the Fundamental Orders, setting up an elected government. The document is often called the first written constitution in the Western tradition.
events.html: Settlers of Hartford, Windsor and Wethersfield agreed the Fundamental Orders, setting up an elected government. The document is often called the first written constitution in the Western tradition.

events.title: Afghan army defeats the Marathas at the Third Battle of Panipat
events.description: Ahmad Shah Durrani's army crushed the Maratha forces north of Delhi in one of the largest battles of the century. The defeat halted Maratha expansion and helped open the way to British power in India.
events.html: Ahmad Shah Durrani's army crushed the Maratha forces north of Delhi in one of the largest battles of the century. The defeat halted Maratha expansion and helped open the way to British power in India.

events.title: Congress ratifies the Treaty of Paris with Great Britain
events.description: Meeting at the Maryland State House in Annapolis, the Confederation Congress proclaimed its ratification of the Treaty of Paris, the official end of the American Revolutionary War. The treaty recognised the colonies as free, sovereign and independent.
events.html: Meeting at the Maryland State House in Annapolis, the Confederation Congress proclaimed its ratification of the Treaty of Paris, the official end of the American Revolutionary War. The treaty recognised the colonies as free, sovereign and independent.

events.title: Bonaparte defeats the Austrian army at Rivoli
events.description: Near Rivoli, then in the Republic of Venice, the outnumbered French Army of Italy under General Napoleon Bonaparte defeated József Alvinczi's Austrians, who were trying to relieve besieged Mantua. Mantua fell in February, and France won the war that year.

events.title: Felice Orsini attempts to assassinate Napoleon III
events.description: The Italian nationalist Orsini and his accomplices threw bombs at the Emperor's carriage outside the Paris Opéra, killing eight people. Napoleon III escaped and soon backed Piedmont against Austria.
events.html: The Italian nationalist Orsini and his accomplices threw bombs at the Emperor's carriage outside the Paris Opéra, killing eight people. Napoleon III escaped and soon backed Piedmont against Austria.

events.title: Earthquake and fire destroy much of Kingston, Jamaica
events.description: An earthquake and the fires that followed wrecked Jamaica's capital, killing about 1,000 people. Much of the city's historic core was rebuilt in reinforced concrete.
events.html: An earthquake and the fires that followed wrecked Jamaica's capital, killing about 1,000 people. Much of the city's historic core was rebuilt in reinforced concrete.

events.title: Roosevelt and Churchill meet at Casablanca
events.description: The Casablanca Conference agreed to invade Sicily and intensify the bombing of Germany. At its close Roosevelt announced that the Allies would accept only unconditional surrender.

events.title: Marilyn Monroe marries Joe DiMaggio
events.description: The film star and the retired New York Yankees hero married at San Francisco City Hall. The marriage lasted less than a year, though DiMaggio remained devoted to Monroe until her death.
events.html: The film star and the retired New York Yankees hero married at San Francisco City Hall. The marriage lasted less than a year, though DiMaggio remained devoted to Monroe until her death.

events.title: De Gaulle vetoes Britain's entry into the Common Market
events.description: At a press conference in Paris, Charles de Gaulle rejected Britain's application to join the EEC. He vetoed a second application in 1967, and Britain joined only in 1973.
